statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail risk 3% (low) with no Nasdaq-100 price path observable inside the CME weekend halt, which ends at the 22:00Z reopen roughly half an hour after this assessment, against Stress of 71% (high) as the Strait of Hormuz stays closed on Iran's seven stated conditions and the weekend escalation stack widened into Yemen, Saudi Arabia and a third US carrier deployment.
recommendation: Tail remains far below the block threshold, so the mapped policy state stays EA_ON. A narrow danger window is published across the 22:00Z CME reopen and the hour after it, 00:00-02:00 Berlin on 5 October, where the published forecast Tail path reaches the WATCH band on weekend-gap and thin-liquidity grounds rather than on observed one-way structure. Existing-position management and emergency protection remain unaffected by this state.
headline: Tail holds its 3% halt floor with the 22:00Z CME reopen under an hour away as a widening Yemen and Saudi escalation stack lifts Stress to 71%
body:
CME equity-index futures have been halted since Friday 21:00Z and reopen at 22:00Z on 4 October, roughly half an hour after this assessment. The current clock-hour window ends exactly at that reopen, so it contains no tradeable Nasdaq-100 price path at all and Tail stays at its structural floor of 3%. The last observed structure was orderly and two-way: the cash index set a record intraday high of 31,017.53 on Friday 2 October, surrendered it in full, and closed at a record 30,807.93, up 1.00% from a 30,501.60 previous close, inside a 30,737.07-31,017.53 range. December NQ futures settled at 31,049, up 0.94%, which is the reference for any weekend gap. A record close that gives back its own high is the opposite of the no-retracement path Tail is designed to measure.

Stress rises two points to 71% because the weekend escalation stack widened again while the market could not price it. Iran's parliament speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf repeated that the Strait of Hormuz will not reopen until seven conditions are met, and Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi paired diplomacy with a warning that Tehran is "more prepared than before". Monitoring recorded a single transit on 27 September against a pre-crisis baseline near 85 a day, and the count of AIS-visible vessels holding position away from working ports rose to 236 as of 20:50Z from 218 earlier in the day. During Sunday, explosions were reported near Qeshm and Sirik and a tanker reported multiple explosions about 60 nautical miles south of Al Mukha, Yemen; the Houthis claimed ballistic-missile and drone strikes on Saudi Aramco facilities at Khurais and Riyadh; Yemen's Saudi-backed Presidential Council announced ground operations against Houthi-held territory; reporting described additional US forces heading to Israel and a third US carrier strike group moving toward the region; and Iran's oil minister Mohsen Paknejad resigned, with NIOC chief executive Hamid Bovard named acting minister.

Cross-assets still conflict rather than align, which under this contract raises Stress and uncertainty instead of Tail. September payrolls rose 29,000 against roughly a 90,000 consensus and unemployment edged to 4.2%, yet the 2-year yield ended Friday up at 4.837% and the 10-year at 5.279% after an initial fall. The Federal Reserve H.15 release shows the 2-year at 4.78% and the 10-year at 5.24% for 1 October, both lower on the day. VIX fell 6.59% to 15.31 from a 16.39 previous close, finishing near its 15.30 session low, while WTI eased 1.90% to $91.11 and Brent held near $102.25, essentially unchanged, after the G7 agreed to deploy 100 million barrels of reserves over four months and OPEC+ left November targets unchanged. Low volatility and a flat-to-softer crude complex alongside a shut strait and claimed strikes on Saudi infrastructure is conflict, not the aligned amplifier stack Tail requires.

The published forecast therefore keeps every hour in EA_ON except the 22:00Z reopen and the hour after it, where Tail is raised to 22% and 20% inside the WATCH band and the danger window is drawn. That step is conditional on an untested reopen into thin Sunday liquidity, not on observed one-way structure, and an early genuine retracement would invalidate it. Tail then decays to an 8% to 10% range through the Asian and European sessions, rebuilds to 10% into the US pre-market, reaches 15% at the 13:30Z cash open, peaks at 17% for the 14:00Z ISM Services PMI, and eases to 11% by the final published hour at the 20:00Z cash close. September CPI was verified as scheduled for 14 October, outside this seven-day window, so it is not carried in the event calendar. The shared Finviz context file was last collected on 29 September with a partial collection status, so it is far outside the 90-minute freshness rule and was not used as evidence; this assessment rests on independently verified sources.

lookbackSummary: Across the past 24 published hours Claude held Tail at 3% in every slot, with every hour mapping to EA_ON and green and the dominant mode normal throughout, reflecting a market that was either in orderly two-way trade or closed for the weekend. Stress rose from 69% at 21:00Z on 3 October to a 79% ceiling at 09:00Z on 4 October as the weekend Hormuz checkpoints opened, then eased through the 73%, 70%, 68%, 66% and 64% readings of the European and US-equivalent hours before rebuilding into a 66% to 69% band through the Sunday evening as the Yemen and Saudi incident flow accumulated. Confidence ran between 83% and 88%, improving through the Sunday hours as current levels, yields, oil and the forward calendar were re-verified while the live price path stayed structurally unavailable inside the weekend halt.
outlookSummary: The current hour is wholly inside the CME halt and ends at the reopen instant, so it carries no scoreable Nasdaq-100 structure and Tail is held at 3% while Stress sits at 71% on the closed strait and the widening Yemen and Saudi incident flow. Tail is then raised to 22% and 20%, inside the WATCH band, across the 22:00Z reopen and the hour after it, which the published danger window covers; that step reflects weekend-gap and thin-liquidity hazard rather than observed one-way structure, and an early orderly retracement would invalidate it. Tail falls back to 12% once Asian depth returns and decays to an 8% to 10% range through the Asian and European sessions, rebuilds to 10% into the US pre-market, reaches 15% at the 13:30Z cash open, peaks at 17% for the 14:00Z ISM Services PMI release window, then eases through the afternoon to 11% across the power hour and the 20:00Z cash close. Stress trends down from 73% at the reopen to 61% by the end of the horizon and Confidence eases from 86% to 77% as the distance from this assessment's evidence cutoff grows. Every forecast hour outside the two reopen slots maps to EA_ON and green.
